create.name: Bhante Bodhidhamma
create.bio:
Bhante Bodhidhamma is an English Theravada monk who teaches insight meditation in the line of the Burmese master Mahasi Sayadaw. Born Peter Ridley in 1947 and raised a Catholic, he came to Buddhism through Soto Zen practice in Birmingham at the end of the 1970s, then turned to vipassana, training with Sayadaw U Janaka in Myanmar and later with Sayadaw U Pandita. He took monastic ordination in Birmingham in 1986 and spent about eight years living alone in a hut at Kanduboda, a Mahasi meditation centre in Sri Lanka, before coming back to Britain in 1998.

After teaching around England and Ireland he served as resident teacher at Gaia House in Devon from 2001 to 2004, and in 2007 opened Satipanya, a small retreat centre in the Shropshire hills close to the Welsh border, where he is spiritual director alongside Noirin Sheahan. Retreats there follow the Mahasi method of noting each experience as it arises and moving slowly, in silence, with daily interviews, and close with loving-kindness practice; everything is offered on a donation basis. He also runs online courses on carrying practice into everyday life, sits with students in an online meditation hall, and shares guided meditations and hundreds of recorded talks through Satipanya's website, its YouTube channel and Dharma Seed.

courses.title: Two Week Winter Retreat with Bhante Bodhidhamma
courses.description: A residential Mahasi insight retreat at Satipanya, taken as one or two weeks, for people who have already done at least a week-long Mahasi course. Days alternate sitting and walking practice in silence, with regular teacher interviews. Retreats run on donations, with a daily deposit to hold a place.

courses.title: Online Wintertime Practice in Ordinary Daily Life
courses.description: An online winter course on Zoom about taking meditation into work, relationships and daily routines. Each week opens with a day of sitting, walking and loving-kindness practice, after which participants set their own commitments and meet again the following Sunday to review them.

free_resources.title: Guided meditations led by Bhante Bodhidhamma
free_resources.description: Free audio guidance for insight meditation, from a short introduction to vipassana to longer detailed and assisted sittings, body-awareness and loving-kindness practices, all downloadable from the Satipanya website.

free_resources.title: A Foundation Course in Buddhism
free_resources.description: A free series of recorded talks that works through the Four Noble Truths, covering suffering, the three characteristics, dependent origination, kamma, ethics and the development of the mind.

free_resources.title: Online Meditation Hall
free_resources.description: Free morning and evening group sits on Zoom with Pali chanting and loving-kindness, open to people who have done at least one day of Mahasi practice; Bhante or Noirin Sheahan join when they can.

free_resources.title: Meditation in Ordinary Daily Life
free_resources.description: A free essay by Bhante on extending mindfulness from the cushion into every activity of the day, drawing on the Buddha's teaching on clear comprehension.

Email decoded from Cloudflare protection on the Satipanya contact page (bodhidhamma@satipanya.org.uk); it is the centre's address for him as spiritual director.
Base: Satipanya's published postal address is White Grit, Minsterley, Shropshire (England, near the Welsh border); the queue entry said 'Welsh borders'. City set to Minsterley, the postal town.
Gaia House is not a Spiritpedia listing yet, so teaches_at is empty; he was its resident teacher 2001-2004 and is on its teacher list, but no 2026-27 Gaia House programme with him was found.
Satipanya is co-led with Noirin Sheahan; the YouTube channel, website and calendar are the centre's, though the videos chosen were checked to be his talks (name label on each thumbnail).
Prices: retreats are on dana; the calendar says the deposit rises to £25 a day from January 2027. The winter retreat URL is a calendar anchor because the retreat has no page of its own.
Dated online events are in the 2027 section of the Satipanya calendar (Wintertime weeks begin 10 January and 14 February 2027); dates on the Wintertime page itself are from an earlier year.
